## Load packages

```{r loading packages}
#Checks if each package is installed; installs it if not, then loads
#it either way
packages <- c("here", "dplyr", "glue", "janitor", "ggplot2", "DT", "scales", "stringr")
for (p in packages) {
  if (p %in% rownames(installed.packages())) {
    library(p, character.only = TRUE)
  } else {
    install.packages(p)
    library(p, character.only = TRUE)
  }
}
#rCAX isn't on CRAN, so it needs a different install method
if (!"rCAX" %in% rownames(installed.packages())) {
  if (!"remotes" %in% rownames(installed.packages())) install.packages("remotes")
  remotes::install_github("nwfsc-cb/rCAX")
}
library(rCAX)

#Registers Times New Roman with the Windows graphics device so
#ggplot2's theme() can actually resolve the font
windowsFonts(`Times New Roman` = windowsFont("TT Times New Roman"))
```

## Define data loading and cleaning function

```{r define function}
#Pulls a StreamNet HLI table via rCAX, filtered to a single ESU/DPS.
#Defaults are RperS (recruits per spawner) for Upper Columbia spring
#Chinook, but hli_type/esudps_sel can target a different table/population
hli_pull_clean <- function(hli_type = "RperS",
                            esudps_sel = "Salmon, Chinook (Upper Columbia River spring-run ESU)"){
  cat(glue("loading {hli_type} data for {esudps_sel}\n"))
  
  hli_raw <- rcax_hli(
    hli_type,
    flist = list(esudps = esudps_sel)
  )
  #rpers = recruits per spawner; totalspawners = all-origin spawner
  #abundance; hatcheryspawners = hatchery-origin spawner abundance
  hli_clean <- hli_raw %>%
    clean_names() %>%
    mutate(
      rpers = as.numeric(rpers),
      totalspawners = as.numeric(totalspawners),
      recruits = as.numeric(recruits),
      hatcheryspawners = as.numeric(hatcheryspawners)
    )
  
  cat(glue("pulled {nrow(hli_clean)} rows\n"))
  return(hli_clean)
}
```

## Call function for each subset of interest

```{r call function all subsets}
upper_col_sp_chin_rpers <- hli_pull_clean()
snake_sp_su_chin_rpers <- hli_pull_clean(esudps_sel = "Salmon, Chinook (Snake River spring/summer-run ESU)")

snake_steelhead_rpers <- hli_pull_clean(esudps_sel = "Steelhead (Snake River Basin DPS)")
```

## Explore additional data issues, produce summaries, and visualize

```{r define exploration functions}
#Missingness by column
na_summary_function <- function(data){
  data.frame(column_name = colnames(data), n_missing = colSums(is.na(data)))
}

#Summary stats for the rpers column
rpers_summary_function <- function(data){
  summary(data$rpers)
}

#Collection methods reported per population, so agency/protocol
#coverage is visible at a glance
rpers_methods_summary_function <- function(data){
  data %>%
    filter(!is.na(protmethname)) %>%
    select(populationname, agency, protmethname) %>%
    unique() %>%
    arrange(populationname)
}

#Flags population/spawningyear combos with more than one NOSA row -
#happens when two agencies both report the same population/year.
#Diagnostic only; resolved via bestvalue filter below, not here
check_nosa_duplicates <- function(nosa_csv_path, title_label){
  nosa_data <- read.csv(nosa_csv_path)
  dup_check <- nosa_data %>%
    count(populationname, spawningyear) %>%
    filter(n > 1)
  cat(glue("{title_label}: {nrow(dup_check)} duplicated population/year combinations\n"))
  print(dup_check)
  return(dup_check)
}

#Compares RperS total spawner estimates against NOSA. Both inputs are
#filtered to bestvalue == "Yes" first, so only one agency's row per
#population/year is used in the join
compare_rpers_nosa_function <- function(rpers_data, nosa_csv_path, pop_label, title_label){
  nosa_for_comparison <- read.csv(nosa_csv_path) %>%
    filter(bestvalue == "Yes") %>%
    select(populationname, spawningyear, tsaij, nosaij,
           nosa_agency = agency, nosa_protmethname = protmethname,
           nosa_methodadjustments = methodadjustments)
  
  #Checks whether RperS totalspawners matches NOSA tsaij, and whether
  #NOSA natural-origin spawners plus RperS hatchery-origin spawners
  #sum to RperS totalspawners
  rpers_nosa_compare <- rpers_data %>%
    filter(bestvalue == "Yes") %>%
    select(populationname, broodyear, totalspawners, hatcheryspawners,
           rpers_agency = agency, rpers_protmethname = protmethname,
           rpers_methodadjustments = methodadjustments) %>%
    left_join(nosa_for_comparison, by = c("populationname" = "populationname", "broodyear" = "spawningyear")) %>%
    mutate(
      total_spawners_diff = totalspawners - tsaij,
      total_spawners_pct_diff = round((total_spawners_diff / tsaij) * 100, 1),
      natural_plus_hatchery = nosaij + hatcheryspawners,
      sum_check_diff = totalspawners - natural_plus_hatchery,
      sum_check_pct_diff = round((sum_check_diff / totalspawners) * 100, 1)
    )
  
  if (nrow(rpers_nosa_compare) > nrow(rpers_data %>% filter(bestvalue == "Yes"))) {
    cat(glue("Warning: comparison table has {nrow(rpers_nosa_compare)} rows, more than the {nrow(rpers_data %>% filter(bestvalue == 'Yes'))} bestvalue-filtered RperS rows going in\n"))
  }
  
  print(datatable(rpers_nosa_compare))
  print(summary(rpers_nosa_compare$total_spawners_diff))
  print(summary(rpers_nosa_compare$total_spawners_pct_diff))
  print(summary(rpers_nosa_compare$sum_check_diff))
  print(summary(rpers_nosa_compare$sum_check_pct_diff))
  
  return(rpers_nosa_compare)
}
```

```{r define presentation theme and export function}
#Presentation theme sized for a full-bleed 16:9 slide
presentation_theme <- theme(
  text = element_text(family = "Times New Roman", face = "bold", size = 22),
  plot.title = element_text(size = 28, face = "bold"),
  axis.title = element_text(size = 22),
  axis.text = element_text(size = 18),
  strip.text = element_text(size = 18),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 18),
  legend.title = element_text(size = 20)
)

#Exports at full-bleed 16:9 widescreen dimensions
ggsave_presentation <- function(filename, height = 7.5, width = 13.33, dpi = 300){
  ggsave(here("Results", "Figures", filename), height = height, width = width, dpi = dpi)
}

#Wraps a title string to a fixed character width, breaking into as
#many lines as needed
wrap_title <- function(text, width = 28){
  paste(strwrap(text, width = width), collapse = "\n")
}

#Splits populationname into location_name and run_species. Most names
#use " - " as a separator; some have no dash and instead end in a
#run/species phrase, which is matched and stripped separately
split_pop_name <- function(df){
  split_cols <- stringr::str_split_fixed(df$populationname, " - ", n = 2)
  
  location_name <- split_cols[, 1]
  run_species <- split_cols[, 2]
  
  run_species_patterns <- c(
    "spring Chinook Salmon", "summer Chinook Salmon", "fall Chinook Salmon",
    "spring/summer Chinook Salmon", "summer Steelhead", "spring Steelhead"
  )
  
  no_dash <- run_species == ""
  
  for (pattern in run_species_patterns) {
    matches <- no_dash & endsWith(location_name, paste0(" ", pattern))
    run_species[matches] <- pattern
    location_name[matches] <- trimws(sub(paste0(" ", pattern, "$"), "", location_name[matches]))
  }
  
  df %>%
    mutate(
      location_name = location_name,
      run_species = run_species
    )
}
```

```{r define visualization functions}
#Faceted bar plot of total spawner abundance by population and brood
#year. Filtered to bestvalue == "Yes" so duplicate agency rows for the
#same population/year don't get summed together in geom_col()
plot_totalspawners_function <- function(data, plot_title, file_name){
  data %>%
    filter(bestvalue == "Yes") %>%
    split_pop_name() %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = broodyear, y = totalspawners, fill = location_name)) +
    geom_col() +
    facet_wrap(~ location_name, ncol = 3) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
    labs(title = plot_title, x = "Brood Year", y = "Total Spawners") +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    presentation_theme
  ggsave_presentation(file_name)
}

#Plots RperS totalspawners against NOSA tsaij directly, so any
#systematic mismatch is visible at a glance. compare_data is already
#filtered to bestvalue == "Yes", so duplicate-agency points don't stack
plot_rpers_nosa_compare_function <- function(compare_data, title_label, pop_label){
  compare_plot <- compare_data %>%
    split_pop_name() %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = broodyear)) +
    geom_line(aes(y = totalspawners, linetype = "RperS (totalspawners)"), linewidth = 1, color = "red") +
    geom_point(aes(y = totalspawners), size = 2, color = "red") +
    geom_line(aes(y = tsaij, linetype = "NOSA (tsaij)"), linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.5, color = "blue") +
    geom_point(aes(y = tsaij), size = 2, alpha = 0.5, color = "blue") +
    facet_wrap(~ location_name, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
    labs(title = glue("Total Spawner Abundance: RperS vs. NOSA\nby Population and Year ({title_label})"),
         x = "Year", y = "Total Spawner Abundance", linetype = "Source") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    presentation_theme +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 13))
  print(compare_plot)
  ggsave_presentation(glue("rpers_vs_nosa_totspawners_by_pop_year_{pop_label}.png"))
}

#Data coverage timeline: blue = rpers present, dark red = row exists
#but rpers is NA, light red = no row at all for that population/year.
#Filtered to bestvalue == "Yes" so a duplicate agency row doesn't
#register as "data available" independently of the primary row
coverage_rpers_function <- function(data, title_label, file_name){
  pop_data <- data %>%
    filter(bestvalue == "Yes") %>%
    filter(!is.na(broodyear)) %>%
    split_pop_name() %>%
    select(location_name, broodyear, rpers)
  
  year_range <- seq(min(pop_data$broodyear), max(pop_data$broodyear))
  populations <- unique(pop_data$location_name)
  
  full_grid <- data.frame()
  for (pop in populations) {
    full_grid <- bind_rows(full_grid, data.frame(location_name = pop, broodyear = year_range))
  }
  
  pop_data_summary <- pop_data %>%
    group_by(location_name, broodyear) %>%
    summarize(has_row = TRUE, has_value = any(!is.na(rpers)), .groups = "drop")
  
  data_status <- full_grid %>%
    left_join(pop_data_summary, by = c("location_name", "broodyear")) %>%
    mutate(
      status = case_when(
        is.na(has_row) ~ "No data reported",
        has_value ~ "Data available",
        TRUE ~ "NA"
      )
    )
  
  plot_title <- wrap_title(glue("RperS Data Availability - {title_label}"))
  
  data_status %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = broodyear, y = location_name, fill = status)) +
    geom_tile(height = 0.9, width = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(
      "Data available" = "blue",
      "NA" = "darkred",
      "No data reported" = "lightcoral"
    )) +
    labs(title = plot_title, x = "Year", y = NULL, fill = "Status") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
    presentation_theme +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 22))
  
  ggsave_presentation(file_name)
}

#Data coverage colored by collection method. Filtered to
#bestvalue == "Yes" so a duplicate agency's method doesn't get
#counted alongside the primary row's method for the same year
coverage_by_method_function <- function(data, plot_title, file_name){
  method_data <- data %>%
    filter(bestvalue == "Yes") %>%
    mutate(protmethname = as.character(protmethname)) %>%
    split_pop_name() %>%
    filter(!is.na(protmethname), !is.na(year)) %>%
    select(location_name, year, protmethname) %>%
    unique()
  
  method_counts <- method_data %>%
    count(location_name, year)
  
  method_labeled <- method_data %>%
    left_join(method_counts, by = c("location_name", "year")) %>%
    mutate(
      method_label = case_when(
        n > 1 ~ "Multiple Methods",
        TRUE ~ protmethname
      )
    ) %>%
    select(location_name, year, method_label) %>%
    unique()
  
  method_labeled %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = year, y = location_name, fill = method_label)) +
    geom_tile(height = 0.9, width = 1) +
    labs(title = plot_title, x = "Year", y = NULL, fill = "Collection Method") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
    presentation_theme
  
  ggsave_presentation(file_name)
}
```
